request.system:
You read a slice of a team chat channel and split it into episodes.

An episode is one conversation about one topic: a question and its answers, an
incident and its fix, a decision being made. Conversations in a busy channel
interleave, so an episode's messages need not be consecutive. Leave out messages
that belong to no real conversation (greetings, "thanks!", off-topic chatter).

For each episode give:
- title: under 8 words, specific ("CSV export times out for large orgs", not "Export issue")
- status: "resolved" if the conversation reached an answer or fix, "open" if it
  ended without one, "info" if it was an announcement or FYI
- message_ids: every message that belongs to it, using the IDs in square brackets
- points: 1 to 4 short sentences summarising what happened. Each point lists in
  "cites" the IDs of the messages that support it. Only cite messages in the same
  episode. A point you cannot support with a message should not be written.

Use only what the messages say. Do not guess at causes or outcomes that nobody stated.

messages.content:
--- 2026-03-03 (UTC) ---
[1772530200.000124] 09:30 kim: Brightside reports duplicate invoices created from their Stripe webhook, roughly 1 in 50
[1772530380.000125] 09:33 priya: probably Stripe retrying after a slow response from us. Do the duplicates have the same Stripe event ID?
[1772530560.000126] 09:36 dana: unrelated but three customers this week asked for a dark mode. Is that on the roadmap?
[1772530680.000127] 09:38 kim: yes, same event ID on each pair
[1772530800.000128] 09:40 lee: dark mode isn't planned this quarter. Can you add those customers to the feature request so we can count them?
[1772530860.000129] 09:41 priya: then we're not deduplicating on event ID. I'll add an idempotency check keyed on it.
[1772530980.000130] 09:43 dana: will do
[1772531100.000131] 09:45 mo: lunch order going in at 11 if anyone wants in
[1772533200.000132] 10:20 priya: idempotency check is live. Replayed yesterday's events on staging and got zero duplicates.
[1772533440.000133] 10:24 kim: I'll tell Brightside, and they can delete the existing duplicates from the invoices list
